title: Magnetic Fields due to Electric Current
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: State Biot-Savart Law in vector and scalar forms.
cards.a:
Vector form: d B = (μ₀ / 4π) · [ I (d l × r) / r³ ]
Scalar form: dB = (μ₀ / 4π) · (I dl sin θ / r²), where θ is angle between current element I dl and position vector r.
cards.hint: Constant: μ₀ / 4π = 10⁻⁷ T·m/A (or Wb/A·m). Permeability of free space: μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

cards.q: Magnetic field B due to an infinitely long straight wire carrying current I?
cards.a: B = μ₀ I / (2 π r), where r is perpendicular distance from the wire.
cards.hint: For a semi-infinite wire (point opposite to one end): B = μ₀ I / (4 π r).

cards.q: Magnetic field B at the center of a circular coil of N turns and radius R?
cards.a:
B = μ₀ N I / (2 R).
For a circular arc subtending angle θ (in radians) at center: B = (μ₀ I / 4π R) · θ.
cards.hint: For a semi-circular loop (θ = π): B = μ₀ I / (4 R); for a quadrant (θ = π/2): B = μ₀ I / (8 R).

cards.q: Magnetic field B along the axis of a circular current loop at distance x from center?
cards.a:
B_axis = [ μ₀ N I R² ] / [ 2 (R² + x²)^(3/2) ].
At center (x = 0): B_center = μ₀ N I / (2 R).
At large distance (x ≫ R): B_axis ≈ [ μ₀ (2 M) ] / [ 4π x³ ], where M = N I A = N I π R² is magnetic dipole moment.
cards.hint: Ratio of field at center to field at distance x = R: B_center / B_axis = (1 + 1)^(3/2) = 2^(3/2) = 2√2 ≈ 2.83.

cards.q: At what axial distance x from center of circular coil is B equal to B_center / 8?
cards.a:
x = R √3.
B_axis / B_center = R³ / (R² + x²)^(3/2) = 1/8 = (1/2)³ ⇒ (R² + x²)^(1/2) = 2 R ⇒ R² + x² = 4 R² ⇒ x = R √3.
cards.hint: Top MHT-CET numerical! Memorize: at x = R√3, field drops to 1/8 of central value.

cards.q: State Ampere's Circuital Law and its mathematical equation.
cards.a: The line integral of magnetic field B around any closed loop (Amperian loop) equals μ₀ times the total net electric current enclosed by the loop: ∮ B · dl = μ₀ · I_enclosed.
cards.hint: Magnetic analogue of Gauss's Law in electrostatics. Valid for steady currents.

cards.q: Magnetic field B inside an ideal long Solenoid and Toroid?
cards.a:
Solenoid (inside): B = μ₀ n I = μ₀ (N / L) I.
Solenoid (at extreme ends): B_end = (1/2) μ₀ n I.
Toroid (inside core of mean radius r): B = μ₀ n I = μ₀ [ N / (2π r) ] I.
cards.hint: n = N/L is turns per unit length. Magnetic field outside an ideal solenoid or toroid is ZERO.

cards.q: Lorentz Force on a charged particle q moving with velocity v in electric and magnetic fields?
cards.a:
Total Lorentz Force: F = q (E + v × B).
Magnetic force: F_m = q (v × B) ⇒ F_m = q v B sin θ.
cards.hint: Magnetic force is ALWAYS perpendicular to velocity v, so work done by magnetic force on a charge is strictly ZERO (speed and KE remain constant).

cards.q: Motion of a charged particle entering perpendicular (θ = 90°) to a uniform magnetic field B?
cards.a:
Path: Uniform CIRCULAR motion.
Radius: r = m v / (q B) = p / (q B) = √(2 m K) / (q B).
Time Period: T = 2 π m / (q B) (completely independent of speed v and radius r!).
Cyclotron frequency: f = q B / (2 π m).
cards.hint: T and f do NOT depend on velocity or orbit radius! This is the fundamental resonance principle of the Cyclotron.

cards.q: Helical path of a charged particle entering magnetic field at an arbitrary angle θ (0 < θ < 90°)?
cards.a:
Radius of helix: r = m v_⊥ / (q B) = (m v sin θ) / (q B).
Pitch of helix (linear distance moved per revolution along field): p = v_∥ · T = (v cos θ) · [ 2 π m / (q B) ].
cards.hint: Parallel velocity component v_∥ = v cos θ causes linear translation; perpendicular component v_⊥ = v sin θ causes circular motion.

cards.q: Velocity Selector: Condition for an undeflected charged particle?
cards.a:
Electric and magnetic fields are crossed (perpendicular to each other and to velocity v).
Condition: q E = q v B ⇒ v = E / B.
cards.hint: Only particles with the exact speed v = E/B pass straight without deflection.

cards.q: Magnetic force on a current-carrying straight conductor of length L in uniform field B?
cards.a: F = I (L × B) ⇒ F = I L B sin θ, where θ is angle between current direction L and field B.
cards.hint: Direction of force is given by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule or Right-Hand Palm Rule. Force is zero if wire is parallel to field (θ = 0°).

cards.q: Force per unit length between two infinitely long parallel current-carrying wires separated by distance d?
cards.a:
F / L = (μ₀ I₁ I₂) / (2 π d).
Like currents (same direction): ATTRACT each other.
Unlike currents (opposite directions): REPEL each other.
cards.hint: Opposite to electrostatic charges! (Like charges repel, but like currents attract!).

cards.q: SI definition of 1 Ampere based on force between parallel wires?
cards.a: 1 Ampere is that constant current which, when maintained in each of two infinitely long, parallel, straight conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces between them a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre of length.
cards.hint: Derived from F/L = μ₀ I₁ I₂ / (2π d) = (4π × 10⁻⁷ × 1 × 1) / (2π × 1) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ N/m.

cards.q: Torque on a planar current loop of area A and N turns in a uniform magnetic field B?
cards.a: τ = M × B ⇒ τ = M B sin θ = N I A B sin θ, where M = N I A is magnetic dipole moment and θ is angle between normal to loop and field B.
cards.hint: Maximum torque at θ = 90° (plane of coil parallel to field B); zero torque at θ = 0° (plane of coil perpendicular to field B).

cards.q: Moving Coil Galvanometer (MCG): Working principle and equilibrium condition?
cards.a:
Principle: A current-carrying coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a deflecting torque.
Deflecting Torque = Restoring Torque: N I A B = c θ ⇒ I = (c / N A B) · θ ⇒ I ∝ θ.
cards.hint: c is restoring torque per unit twist of phosphor-bronze suspension wire; θ is angular deflection.

cards.q: Why is a RADIAL magnetic field used in a Moving Coil Galvanometer and how is it produced?
cards.a:
Purpose: Keeps plane of coil always PARALLEL to magnetic field lines (θ = 90°, sin θ = 1) in all positions, making deflection θ directly linear with current I (I ∝ θ).
Produced by: (1) Cylindrical concave magnetic pole pieces, and (2) a soft iron cylindrical core placed between the poles.
cards.hint: Essential 2-mark HSC Board question! Eliminates non-linear sin θ dependence, giving an evenly spaced linear scale.

cards.q: Current Sensitivity and Voltage Sensitivity of a Moving Coil Galvanometer?
cards.a:
Current Sensitivity: S_i = θ / I = N A B / c (SI unit: rad/A or div/A).
Voltage Sensitivity: S_v = θ / V = θ / (I R) = S_i / R = N A B / (c R) (SI unit: rad/V or div/V).
cards.hint: Doubling N doubles Current Sensitivity S_i, but may NOT change Voltage Sensitivity S_v because coil resistance R also doubles!

cards.q: Magnetic Dipole Moment of an electron revolving in an orbit of radius r with speed v?
cards.a: M = (1/2) e v r = e L / (2 m_e), where L = m_e v r is orbital angular momentum.
cards.hint: Orbital current I = e / T = e v / (2π r). Area A = π r² ⇒ M = I A = (1/2) e v r.

cards.q: What is the Gyromagnetic Ratio and Bohr Magneton?
cards.a:
Gyromagnetic Ratio: Ratio of magnetic dipole moment to angular momentum: M / L = e / (2 m_e) ≈ 8.8 × 10¹⁰ C/kg (constant for all electrons!).
Bohr Magneton (μ_B): Minimum magnetic moment of electron in 1st Bohr orbit (L = h / 2π):
μ_B = e h / (4π m_e) ≈ 9.274 × 10⁻²⁴ A·m² (or J/T).
cards.hint: Fundamental natural quantum of atomic magnetic dipole moment.

cards.q: Work done in rotating a magnetic dipole M from angle θ₁ to θ₂ in a magnetic field B?
cards.a:
W = ∫ τ dθ = M B (cos θ₁ - cos θ₂).
From stable equilibrium (θ₁ = 0°) to θ₂ = 180°: W = M B [ 1 - (-1) ] = 2 M B.
cards.hint: Potential energy of dipole is U = - M · B = - M B cos θ.

cards.q: Magnetic field at a distance r inside a solid cylindrical conductor of radius R carrying uniform current I?
cards.a:
Inside (r < R): B = (μ₀ I r) / (2 π R²) ⇒ B ∝ r (linearly increasing from 0 at axis to maximum at surface).
Outside (r ≥ R): B = (μ₀ I) / (2 π r) ⇒ B ∝ 1/r.
cards.hint: B is zero at the central axis (r = 0) and reaches its maximum at the outer surface (r = R).

cards.q: A circular coil of radius R carries current I. If it is unwound and rewound into a coil of 2 turns of radius R/2 carrying same current, how does central field change?
cards.a:
Central field becomes 4 TIMES the original field (B' = 4 B)!
B_original = μ₀ I / (2 R). New turns N' = 2, radius R' = R/2 ⇒ B' = μ₀ (2) I / [ 2 (R/2) ] = 4 [ μ₀ I / (2 R) ] = 4 B.
cards.hint: In general, for n turns of radius R/n from the same wire: B' = n² · B.

cards.q: Helmholtz Coils: Arrangement and purpose?
cards.a:
Two identical, coaxial circular coils separated by a distance exactly equal to their radius (d = R), carrying current in the same direction.
Purpose: Produces an exceptionally UNIFORM magnetic field over a wide region midway between the two coils.
cards.hint: Resultant magnetic field at midpoint: B = 8 μ₀ N I / (5^(3/2) R) ≈ 0.716 μ₀ N I / R.

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: A stationary electric charge is placed in a strong magnetic field. What magnetic force does it experience?
cards.a:
ZERO force!
Magnetic force is F = q (v × B). Since velocity v = 0, F_m = 0 regardless of how strong the magnetic field is.
cards.hint: A magnetic field exerts force ONLY on MOVING charges, never on stationary charges!
